findings.title: Unescaped embed URL interpolated into raw-HTML post enables stored XSS
findings.body: The source URL is inserted directly into `#{url}` with no HTML or attribute escaping. The post is then stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, so it is never sanitized. URI parsing accepts `'`, `=`, `(` and `)` in the query, so a URL such as `http:///?x'onmouseover='alert(1)` passes `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Nokogiri parses the result into a real `onmouseover` attribute and keeps it in `to_html`. Anyone can trigger this by calling `/embed/best?embed_url=...` with a spoofed Referer, which leaves a script-bearing post on the forum domain. Escape the URL (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) or build the link with Nokogiri.

findings.title: raw_html cook method bypasses all HTML sanitization for imported content
findings.body: When `cook_method == raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` verbatim and skips the normal pipeline that sanitizes HTML. Imported content reaches it unfiltered from two places. The RSS job uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`, so `<script>`, `on*` handlers and `<iframe>` from the feed are stored. The Readability import whitelists `href`/`src` attributes, so `javascript:` URLs pass through. That HTML is rendered as-is in the forum and in the embed view (`raw post.cooked`). Any third-party or compromised content in the feed or blog becomes stored XSS on the Discourse origin. The imported HTML should still be run through a sanitizer/whitelist.

findings.title: Kernel#open on admin-supplied feed URL allows command execution / local file read
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` relies on open-uri's patched `Kernel#open`. That only does an HTTP fetch when the string looks like a `scheme://` URL; otherwise it falls back to plain `Kernel#open`. A value like `|some shell command` runs a subprocess, and `/etc/passwd` reads a local file whose content is then imported as a public topic. The URL is never validated, so an admin (not necessarily a server operator on hosted installs) gets RCE or file disclosure. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or an HTTP client after checking the scheme is http/https.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can create unlimited topics by varying the embed URL
findings.body: Any request with a matching Referer (trivially spoofed outside a browser) enqueues `retrieve_topic` for an arbitrary `embed_url`. The only throttle, in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, is keyed on the exact URL string. Adding a different query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) on the embeddable host therefore bypasses it. Each variant causes a server-side fetch and, if the host returns 200, a new topic via `import_remote`. The job is also enqueued on every hit, including the loading page's 30-second auto-reload. Consider normalizing URLs, rate limiting per IP, and limiting how many new embeds can be created.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: The checks `href.start_with?('/')` and `src.start_with?('/')` also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes and produces `http://bloghost/cdn.example.com/img.png`. Protocol-relative image and CDN links are common in blog/RSS content, so they will be broken in imported posts. Skip values starting with `//`, or resolve properly with `URI.join(url, href)`. The same bug exists in the `img` branch at line 70.

findings.title: Crash when the embedded post has been deleted
findings.body: `post = embed.post` returns nil if a moderator deleted the imported post, because Trashable's default scope hides it. When the feed content later changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError. `PollFeed` loops over all items without rescue, so one deleted embed aborts processing of every later feed item on every hourly run. Handle a missing post explicitly, e.g. skip it or clean up the embed.

findings.title: TopicEmbed created from a failed post leads to NOT NULL violation
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` returns the post object even when saving failed and rolled back; the post then has `errors` and `id`/`topic_id` are nil. `post.present?` is still true, so `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil, ...)` runs. The model validations only check `embed_url`/`content_sha1`, so this reaches the DB and raises on the NOT NULL columns. Check `post.persisted?` / `post.errors.blank?` before creating the embed.

findings.title: RSS items without <content> crash the feed import
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` element. That holds for Atom, but standard RSS 2.0 items usually carry `description`/`content:encoded` instead, so `i.content` is nil and NoMethodError aborts the whole poll. `String#scrub` also only exists in Ruby 2.1+, and nothing in the Gemfile backports it. Fall back to `description`/`content_encoded` and guard against nil.

findings.title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of a URL
findings.body: The throttle calls `setnx` and then `expire` in a separate command. If the process dies or Redis errors between the two calls, the key never expires and that embed URL is treated as 'retrieved recently' forever. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

findings.title: Every retrieval synchronously re-polls and re-imports the entire feed
findings.body: When feed polling is enabled, each cache miss calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline. That downloads the whole feed and runs `TopicEmbed.import` for every item. Together with the per-URL throttle (bypassable via distinct URLs), requests for unknown URLs can repeatedly trigger full feed downloads and imports.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` typo turns the if/else into a modifier conditional
findings.body: `end if` makes the whole if/else block a trailing `if` modifier whose condition is the next compiled ERB statement (the output-buffer append for the following text). The template only renders because that append happens to be truthy. Output is also reordered: the condition is evaluated before the block. This should be a plain `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a prefix of `discourseUrl`. For example, `http://forum.example.co` passes when discourseUrl is `http://forum.example.com/`. A foreign origin can then send `discourse-resize` messages. Compare `e.origin` exactly against the origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.

findings.title: Disqus import loses --category and thread dates and now depends on live HTTP fetches
findings.body: The `--category` option was removed, so existing invocations that pass `-c` will fail. Topics are no longer created with the thread's original `created_at`. Each thread now calls `import_remote`, which fetches the link over the network. Any 404/timeout raises OpenURI::HTTPError and aborts the whole import. Non-http links make `import` return nil, so those threads are silently skipped.

findings.title: URL/username requirement specs pass trivially
findings.body: `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false and is not stubbed to true in the 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples. `poll_feed` is therefore never called no matter what the URL or username checks do, so these tests do not verify the conditions they describe. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` (and the other setting) to true in each case.

findings.title: 'is 404 without an embed_url' never reaches the param check
findings.body: `embeddable_host` is blank by default, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess (403) before `params.require(:embed_url)` runs. The example only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it passes without exercising the missing-parameter path its name describes. There is also no coverage for a referer whose host doesn't match.

findings.title: Unrelated edit of an already-shipped migration adding force: true
findings.body: This PR changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. Editing a released migration has no effect where it has already run. Where it hasn't, it now silently drops any existing `top_topics` table. The new `create_topic_embeds` migration uses `force: true` the same way. The change is unrelated to embedding and should be reverted.

findings.title: embed_url limited to varchar(255)
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` creates a varchar(255) column. Article URLs with long slugs or query strings can exceed this, and PostgreSQL then raises 'value too long' during `TopicEmbed.create!`. That fails the import job, or aborts the feed loop. Use `text`, or validate/truncate the length.
